title: Cross-region SLI consolidation and adaptive token-latency dashboard
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Goal: Build a consolidated observability foundation and Grafana dashboard set that exposes token-level latency SLIs, region-aware golden signals, and an adaptive SLO tiering view used by the on-call and capacity teams to make failover/load-shed decisions. This ticket covers instrumentation schema, ingest pipeline changes, a dashboard wireframe, alerting thresholds, and a phased rollout plan.

Background: Our recent incident (2026-01-27 partial regional overload) exposed gaps: (1) token-level P95/P99 was available only per-shard, (2) region spillovers were not correlated with KV cache hit rates, and (3) existing dashboards were fragmented across teams. We need a single-pane observability surface that ties token latency to admit/evict behavior, per-route SLO burn rates, and adaptive circuit state.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Instrumentation: emit token_latency_ns (histogram buckets) with labels: region, shard_id, route, model_variant, kv_hit (true|false), admission_path (priority|background), and trace_id.
- Sampling: all 1-in-20 requests include full token-level histograms; critical customer routes sample 1-in-5. Correlate sampled traces with request-level metadata.
- Aggregation: produce per-minute rollups for P50/P90/P95/P99 and token throughput by route/region. Store raw histograms for 7d and rollup summaries for 90d.
- Dashboards: new Grafana folder "Cross-region SLOs" with panels: region SLO burn rate, token SLO heatmap (route x region), KV-hit correlation scatter (p99 latency vs kv_hit_rate), admission queue-waterfall, and circuit-state timeline. Each panel links to route-level drilldowns and the runbook.
- Alerts: two alert sets — immediate (P99 breach 3m sustained for critical routes) and trending (burn-rate > 5% of reserve capacity over 1h). Alerts must include suggested actions (scale, reroute, degrade-quantization).
- Rollout: behind a feature flag. Canary to prod region-us-east-1 (2 weeks), then add eu-west-1 (1 week), then global. No customer-facing changes first; observability-only until we validate.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Histogram approach vs per-token logs: histograms reduce cardinality and storage but require careful bucket design to capture multi-modal tail behavior for long-generation sessions. We propose exponential buckets tuned for 1ms-30s token latencies.
- Sampling bias: heavier sampling for critical routes reduces detection time but increases ingestion cost. We will mitigate by dynamic sampling tied to route traffic and recent anomaly scores.
- KV hit labeling: adding kv_hit tag has a small callpath cost on hot paths; we will implement an optimized, inlined accessor in the runtime to avoid additional allocations.
- Query latency: building per-minute rollups reduces dashboard query times; however rollups add complexity to the pipeline. We'll reuse existing metrics-aggregator jobs and shard by region+route to keep queries local.

Runbook & Playbooks: link to the living runbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/slo-failover-runbook and initial playbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/pull/84. The runbook maps alert signatures to actions (scale pool, toggle regional routing, enable degraded-quantization).

Observability artifacts & wireframes:
- Grafana mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/grafana-cross-region-slo (wireframes v1,v2)
- Quick synthetic harness for canary: repo https://github.com/redwood-inference/synthetic-slo-harness (branch eng/275312-adaptive-tiles)
- Dashboards to create: Cross-region SLOs / Token SLO Heatmap / KV-hit Correlation / Admission Waterfall / Circuit State Timeline

Privacy and retention: token-level histograms must never include PII. Confirmed with Privacy: histograms are safe; traces linking to customer IDs are redacted. Storage retention set per policy.

Success metrics:
- Mean time to detect cross-region SLO breaches decreases by 40% in canary region.
- Operator confidence (survey) increases; fewer manual runbook escalations in 30 days.
- Reduced false-positive alerts after tuning (target <10% noise rate on burn-rate alerts).
